newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends bit firmer on fall in stocks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends bit firmer on fall in stocks.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures ended slightly firmer on Monday.
A late fall in the Tokyo stock market provided support for the key contract at 99.24, but large offers placed at 99.25-99.26 kept it from rising further, traders said.
Operators were mostly sidelined in the absence of fresh factors, and awaited results of a 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) auction expected on Tuesday, they said.
The December ended up 0.01 at 99.24 after moving in a range of 99.23 and 99.24. Turnover was 8,359 contracts.
The downside was limited after bargain-hunting stopped the contract's fall at 99.21 on Friday, traders said.
But if the contract breaks below 99.20, it may fall as low as 99.15, some traders said. Others said they were more concerned about a possible short-squeeze.
"Dealers who sold in light of a sharp rise in stocks last Thursday may have to cover shorts if the Nikkei falls further," said a city bank dealer.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended at 18,896.99, down 137.55 points or 0.72 percent.
In the cash money market, the key overnight call rate firmed to 0.49 percent, partly due to banks' fund demand for monthly salary payments.

On Friday, the key overnight rate dropped to 0.48 percent from Thursday's 0.51 after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) supplied enough funds through repurchase agreements to ease banks' strong demand for funds for end-March book closings, traders said. But the BOJ did not conduct such an operation this morning, in line with expectations, they said.
The BOJ conducted a neutral morning operation by buying Treasury bills in an overnight repurchase agreement.

"After the BOJ tried to ease fiscal-year-end fund demand last week, fund suppliers started to suspect that short-term money rates may not rise as much as they had expected towards the year end," another city bank dealer said.

The benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) rate was 0.54 percent, unchanged from Friday. Issued volume was limited to 85 billion yen as banks preferred to wait until they can raise funds by issuing one-month CDs which mature in fiscal 1997/98, traders said.
